bib.title: MAUVE: Measuring the Gap Between Neural Text and Human Text using Divergence Frontiers

question: How can the gap between a text generator's distribution and the human text distribution be measured automatically, capturing both degenerate output and failure to cover human text?
hypothesis: A summary of the whole divergence curve between quantized embeddings of model and human text will rank decoders, model sizes and lengths as known properties and humans expect, and correlate with human judgments better than single-statistic metrics.
contributions: Introduce MAUVE, a comparison measure between neural text and human text.
Show MAUVE quantifies known properties of generated text (length, model size, decoding) more correctly and with fewer restrictions than existing distributional metrics.
Find through human evaluation that MAUVE better correlates with human quality judgements.
Find MAUVE can be highly robust to the choice of quantization, embeddings and scaling; release a pip-installable package.

method.summary: Embed N human and N' model texts with GPT-2 large, jointly quantize with k-means (k=500 after PCA), form histograms, and take the area under the curve of exp(-c KL(Q|R_lambda)) vs exp(-c KL(P|R_lambda)) for mixtures R_lambda = lambda P + (1-lambda) Q, c=5. Validated on web text (GPT-2), news (Grover) and story continuation (fine-tuned GPT-2 medium) against alternative metrics, a 36-pair Mechanical Turk study and discriminator accuracy.
method.task: evaluating open-ended text generation (text completion) against human text

datasets.name: Webtext test set (public analogue of GPT-2 WebText)
datasets.size: 5000 articles; prompt = first 35 tokens; max generation 1024 tokens
datasets.preprocessing: human continuation up to 1024 tokens; for human eval 1831 of 5000 prompts hand-selected as well-formed English, completions truncated to 256 BPE tokens

datasets.name: RealNews (April2019 set)
datasets.source: Zellers et al. Grover; public Grover generations reused
datasets.preprocessing: prompt = headline and metadata (domain, date, authors)

datasets.name: WritingPrompts
datasets.size: 5000 randomly chosen test samples; prompt 50 tokens; max 512 tokens
datasets.split: train for fine-tuning, test for prompts

other.use: features for MAUVE; also external LM for Gen. PPL

models.name: Grover mega / GPT-2 large / BERT discriminators

other.story: frozen GPT-2 large with classification head, 25% test split, regularization by 5-fold CV
other.news: Grover mega fine-tuned with binary head

inference.decoding: ancestral (pure) sampling, greedy, nucleus sampling, top-K, beam search (b=4,8, with/without 4-gram repeat block), adversarial perplexity sampling (first 15% tokens uniform random, remainder greedy to match human running perplexity)
inference.top_p: web text and stories {0.9,0.92,0.95,0.99}; news {0.9,0.92,0.94,0.96,0.98}; best by MAUVE reported
inference.samples: 5000 generations per setting; 5 random seeds for sampling-based methods (s.d. reported); greedy and beam deterministic
inference.prompting: text completion from prefix: 35 tokens (web), 50 tokens (stories), headline+metadata (news)

parameters.k_means_k: 500 default; 100 to 5000 tested in main text, {100,250,500,1000} in C.3.3
parameters.pca: keep 90% explained variance, unit l2 normalization
parameters.kmeans_iters: max 500 iterations, 5 repetitions, best objective, FAISS
parameters.drmm: 3 layers x 10 components per layer, 20 epochs, batch 64, lr gamma0=0.005 constant then quadratic anneal
parameters.lattice: 4-d features, 2-layer MLP with batchnorm, 200 epochs, batch 64, lr 0.1 -> 0.05 at half -> 0.01 at 75%, 744 bins (radius sqrt(50))
parameters.finetune_story: GPT-2 medium, 1 epoch, effective batch 32, block 512, Adam, lr 5e-5, HF defaults

other.hardware: 8 Nvidia Quadro RTX GPUs 24G, one per job; CPU work on Intel i9 2.80GHz 32 vCPU 126G
other.mauve_time: 1-3 min on single CPU core for 5000 generations with cached GPT-2 large states; DRMM 1.75 h; lattice ~5 min on TITAN Xp
other.sample_size: small samples give optimistic MAUVE and higher variance (Fig 7, k=n/10)

metrics.name: MAUVE
metrics.definition: area under divergence curve {(exp(-c KL(Q|R_l)), exp(-c KL(P|R_l)))} with R_l=lP+(1-l)Q on k-means histograms of GPT-2-large embeddings

metrics.name: Generation perplexity
metrics.definition: perplexity of text under GPT-2 large; main paper reports |T(Q)-T(P)|

metrics.name: Zipf coefficient, REP, Distinct-4, Self-BLEU (4-gram, 1000 vs 4999 others), Sparsemax score, JS, epsilon-PPL, Frechet distance
metrics.definition: alternative statistics and LM metrics as defined in C.4 and D.2

metrics.name: Discrimination accuracy
metrics.definition: test accuracy of a trained human-vs-machine classifier

metrics.name: Spearman rank correlation with Bradley-Terry human scores or discriminator accuracy
metrics.definition: rank correlation of metric across (model, decoder) settings

eval.protocol: Pairwise Mechanical Turk human study: 9 players (human + 4 GPT-2 sizes x ancestral/nucleus), 90 comparisons per pair of 36 pairs, 214 workers, USD 0.40 per annotation, 5-point scale (Definitely/Slightly A/B, Tie), ties assigned randomly, annotations under 25 s dropped, three questions (human-like, interesting, sensible); Bradley-Terry fit by Zermelo's algorithm; Spearman vs MAUVE. Sampling results mean +- s.d. over 5 runs.

availability.data: public Webtext, RealNews, WritingPrompts, Grover generations

prompts.text: Which continuation is more interesting or creative, given the context?
Which continuation makes more sense, given the context?
Which continuation is more likely to be written by a human?

evidence.quote: We use DRMM with 3 layers and 10 components per layer for a total of 103 clusters
evidence.where: Sec 4.2 (103 is 10^3 lost superscript; C.3.3 says 1000 components)

results.claim: MAUVE correlates with human-like Bradley-Terry scores far above generation perplexity on web text.
results.setup: Web text, GPT-2 small to xl with ancestral and nucleus sampling, 8 settings, completions up to 256 tokens, 90 ratings per pair
results.quote: MAUVE correlates highly with human judgments of how human-like (0.952), interesting (0.810), and sensible (0.857) the machine text is.
results.note: Baseline 0.810 is generation perplexity; Zipf is 0.833 (Table 5). Interesting 0.810 and sensible 0.857 are in same quote.

results.claim: MAUVE correlates with discriminator accuracy for news.
results.setup: News, Grover base/large/mega, Grover mega discriminator
results.table: Table 5, row % Disc. Acc. News, column MAUVE
results.note: Text says 0.96 for news and 0.89 for stories; best baseline for news is REP 0.792.

results.claim: MAUVE correlates with discriminator accuracy for stories.
results.setup: Story continuation, GPT-2 medium fine-tuned, GPT-2 large frozen discriminator
results.table: Table 5, row % Disc. Acc. Stories, column MAUVE

results.claim: MAUVE ranks decoders greedy < ancestral < nucleus.
results.setup: Web text, GPT-2 xl, 5000 generations; greedy 0.016, ancestral 0.882, nucleus 0.940
results.quote: MAUVE correctly identiﬁes the expected quality relationship, assigning the lowest quality to greedy decoding (.016) followed by ancestral sampling (.882), and the highest quality to nucleus sampling (.940).
results.note: Table 3 as extracted shows 0.02, 0.88, 0.94 (rounded); Table 6 gives 0.016, 0.882, 0.940.

results.claim: Generation perplexity rates degenerate greedy text better than ancestral sampling.
results.quote: generation perplexity rates the highly degenerate greedy-decoded text as better than ancestral sampling (11.324 vs. 19.284)
results.note: Main-paper values are |T(Q)-T(P)| differences from human.

results.claim: MAUVE increases with GPT-2 model size under nucleus sampling.
results.setup: Web text, nucleus sampling; small 0.878, medium 0.915, large 0.936, xl 0.940

results.claim: Adversarial perplexity sampling gets near-perfect generation perplexity but low MAUVE.
results.setup: Web text, GPT-2 xl adversarial decoder
results.table: Table 6, GPT-2 xl, row Adversarial, column MAUVE

results.claim: Beam search is degenerate by MAUVE, better than greedy, and blocking 4-gram repeats helps.
results.setup: Web text, GPT-2 small, 5 seeds for sampling; value shown is the 0.366 cell
results.note: Extracted column order of Table 11 is ambiguous: values 0.008, 0.021, 0.026, 0.366, 0.341; ancestral 0.589, nucleus 0.878.

results.claim: MAUVE with RoBERTa-large and GPT-2-large features rank settings almost identically.
results.setup: Web text, all GPT-2 sizes and decoders
results.quote: Quantitatively, the Spearman rank correlation between them across all model and decoders is 0.993.

results.claim: MAUVE ranking is robust to number of k-means clusters, DRMM and lattice quantization.
results.setup: k from 100 to 5000 vs k=500; DRMM and lattice vs k-means
results.quote: Likewise, MAUVE computed with DRMM or lattice quantization has a near-perfect Spearman correlation of at least 0.99 with k-means.

results.claim: MAUVE falls with generation length for every model, where Frechet distance rises and Gen. PPL is non-monotonic.
results.setup: Web text, GPT-2, nucleus and ancestral sampling, max length 200 to 1000, 5 seeds
results.quote: MAUVE is the only comparison measure which correctly shows this behavior across all models and decoding algorithms.

results.claim: Human raters ranked GPT-2 xl nucleus text below human text with loss probability 0.578.
results.quote: will lose to human text with probability 0.578

results.claim: MAUVE disagrees with humans on some pairs and on Grover large.
results.setup: MAUVE rates GPT-2 medium nucleus above large and xl pure sampling; for Grover large it rates ancestral above nucleus
results.quote: MAUVE rates nucleus sampling with GPT-2 medium as being better than pure sampling from GPT-2 large and xl.

results.claim: Cost: MAUVE with k-means on 5000 generations runs in 1-3 minutes on one CPU core given cached embeddings.
results.setup: Intel i9 2.80GHz single core, GPT-2 large hidden states cached
results.quote: takes 1 −3 minutes on a single core of an Intel i9 CPU

limits: Validated on three English domains with GPT-2 and Grover only; closed-ended tasks (summarization, translation) left to future work.
Human study covers 8 GPT-2 settings with 90 ratings per pair, web text only, crowd workers, completions truncated at 256 tokens.
MAUVE disagrees with humans on some specific comparisons and on Grover large (ancestral above nucleus); authors leave this to future work.
Numerical values depend on k, embedding model, c and sample size (smaller samples give optimistic values); only rankings are stable.
Embedding model inductive biases not studied.
Corpus-level score: needs thousands of generations, scores no single answer and checks no facts (this reading, not stated as a limit).

terms.definition: Q places high mass on text which is unlikely under P.
Q cannot generate text which is plausible under P.
C(P,Q) = {(exp(-c KL(Q|R_l)), exp(-c KL(P|R_l))): R_l = lP+(1-l)Q, l in (0,1)}

Holtzman et al., The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
lineage.note: nucleus sampling and degeneration findings MAUVE is checked against; Gen. PPL, Zipf, Self-BLEU protocols

Martins et al. sparsemax / epsilon-perplexity LM metrics

lineage.note: Frechet distance adapted to GPT-2 features
